interconnectors.name: Eastern Green Link 1 (Torness to Hawthorn Pit)

ai_summary:
Scotland’s electrical grid is operating under exceptionally clean conditions, propelled by robust wind generation reaching 4.4 GW. This surge in renewable output has driven Scottish carbon intensity down to an impressive 32 gCO2/kWh, demonstrating the asset fleet's capacity to decisively displace fossil-fuel generation across the broader Great Britain network. 

However, transmission network limitations continue to impose structural bottlenecks. Total wasted energy currently stands at 217.5 MWh, signaling that north-to-south export capacity along the B6 cross-border boundary is reaching physical constraints. The resulting curtailment, while necessary to maintain transmission stability, reflects lost commercial value and elevated balancing costs under the current National Grid ESO balancing mechanism framework.

To capture this stranded generation, strategic priorities must shift toward regional flexibility and infrastructure reinforcement. Accelerating long-duration energy storage deployment, scaling battery assets at constrained nodes, and expanding localized industrial demand—such as green hydrogen electrolyzers—will be essential to absorb this surplus. Resolving these curtailment friction points will allow operators to fully monetize Scotland's 4.4 GW wind potential, protecting project economics while optimizing the delivery of zero-carbon power to wider demand centers.
